audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[3].side and phases[6].side both read "Skill" while win[3] reads "Lux" and win[6] reads "Orianna" — two answers to the same row. Rows 0, 1, 2, 4 and 5 already agree at Skill.
audit.why: At 4-5 Final Spark (3340) and Lucent Singularity (1100) both out-reach Command: Attack (815), so Lux owns that window. At two items Command: Protect (9s shield) absorbs the poke and Command: Shockwave (110/95/80s) decides fights Lux can only chip.
audit.corrected: phases[3].side -> Lux and phases[6].side -> Orianna, whys rewritten to match in the same proposal.

audit.why: Four spikes, correctly timed at 3-5, level 6, first item and late, and the late entry correctly hands the scaling to Orianna.
audit.corrected: Left the timings; fixed the fabricated ability names inside them.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page wrote "Command Attack" and "Command Shockwave" — Riot's names carry the colon: Command: Attack and Command: Shockwave. It also never states the interaction that decides the lane: Shockwave launches enemies toward the BALL, from 410 range around the ball, so the ball's position is the danger line, not Orianna's.
audit.why: Riot text on Orianna's Q and R, with the 815 / 410 ranges from the kit file. Her Q leaves the ball where it lands, which is why a ball parked in the wave leaves her with no ranged answer to Light Binding.
audit.corrected: Names corrected in spikes[0], spikes[1], content.early and wants.foe[1]; ball-position rule written into breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and the packet flags that the matchup carries no "wait for X before you Y" line anywhere.
audit.why: Command: Attack drops to 3s at rank 5 while Shockwave stays 110/95/80s — those two clocks are the whole sequencing story.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with both cooldowns, the 410 ball radius, and the step-up cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: The titles cover passive weaving and ultimate discipline; the pasted bodies covered neither.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to their own titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT: the cooldowns field carried no cooldown number.
audit.why: An earlier proposal targeted these same fields but its replacement text overshot the +/-10% length rule, so apply-proposals dropped the edit and the defect survived on disk.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to the same meaning inside the length budget, grounded in real ability names and cooldowns from champ-data/_kits: breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — E every wave contact. Bank Manaflow and hold Q for her aggression, not yours.
edits.after: Final Spark out-ranges her 815 Q — E every contact and root the moment her ball is parked in the wave.

edits.before: Late Lux decides fights from a screen away: root the entry, slow the pit, and laser the clump your team froze.
edits.after: Two items in, Command: Protect eats your poke and an 80s Shockwave decides the fights you can only chip at.

edits.before: - Orianna Command: Shockwave: matchup-defining — The fight-flipping wombo — track the ball position like a second enemy. It governs your forward steps. - W Prismatic Barrier spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Command: Shockwave: 110s at rank 1, 80s at rank 3 — track the ball, not her; every forward step you take happens while it sits elsewhere. - Prismatic Barrier is 12s and answers Command: Attack chip, never the wombo. - Final Spark is 60s: spend it on the fight, not the wave.

edits.before: The fight-flipping wombo — track the ball position like a second enemy. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Your E reaches 1100 and her Command: Attack 815 — put the zone on her farm spot and she must walk to the ball to answer.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Illumination lingers for seconds, so every spell you land makes your next auto free damage — and Final Spark refreshes it for another one.

edits.before: Orianna wastes Command: Shockwave — that is your full-commit window.
edits.after: A spent Command: Shockwave gives you 80 seconds minimum to commit.

edits.before: That is Orianna’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Her ball parked on herself means Command: Protect eats the Q.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Final Spark is 60/50/40s and your only answer at 3340 range — spend it on a target Shockwave just grouped, never on a wave.

edits.before: Orianna wins by landing Command: Shockwave, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Orianna wins by walking the ball onto you with Command: Attack, shielding your poke with Protect, and Shockwaving your only root.

edits.before: Both of you are immobile artillery, but if Orianna leaves her ball in the wave to farm you can Light Binding her cleanly - punish every mispositioned ball with Q-E while her Command Attack is on the minions.
edits.after: Both of you are immobile artillery, but if Orianna leaves her ball in the wave to farm you can Light Binding her cleanly - punish every mispositioned ball with Q-E while her Command: Attack is on the minions.

edits.before: Final Spark out-ranges her, but Command Shockwave can peel your engage and set up her jungler; play the poke war and don't step into her ball where a full combo plus Shockwave can trade back.
edits.after: Final Spark out-ranges her, but Command: Shockwave can peel your engage and set up her jungler; play the poke war and stay 410 clear of her ball, where a full combo plus Shockwave trades back.

edits.after: It's a skill-matched artillery mirror early: you trade Q-E pokes with her Command: Attack, and the winner is whoever punishes the other's positioning - catch her when the ball is out on the wave to root her for free.

notes: Two fabricated ability names (Command Attack, Command Shockwave) confirmed against the kit and fixed. The packet's 'no sequencing advice anywhere' defect is answered in breakdown.cooldowns with the 7/6/5/4/3s Q clock against the 110/95/80s R. breakdown.carry, ahead, breakdown.late and breakdown.wave remain structurally templated across this champion's matchups; nothing in Orianna's kit gives them enemy-specific content beyond what the cooldowns and dos/donts now carry, so they were left rather than invented. QA re-scope: previous edits to breakdown.cooldowns were rejected for length drift; re-proposed within budget. Cooldowns quoted are Riot per-rank values from the kit files; no spell-shield, cleanse or minion-block behaviour is asserted anywhere, since the kits do not state it.
